messages:
nina-ml: Heads-up — the nightly checkpoint-cleanup cron failed on prod this morning. Job ID chk-20260314-03. Logs show EACCES when removing /mnt/checkpoints/sha-abc. Can someone rerun and bisect? I'm OOO for lunch in ~30m.

sam-eng: ACK. Can you paste the failing log lines?

nina-ml: ````
rm: cannot remove '/mnt/checkpoints/sha-abc': Permission denied
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/cleanup.py\", line 142, in remove_path
    os.remove(p)
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/mnt/checkpoints/sha-abc'
Caused by: chown failed: Operation not permitted
Exit code: 1
````

infra-bot: Alert: cron:checkpoint-cleanup failed (job_id=chk-20260314-03) exit_code=1 — https://ci.redwood/s/34233

kevin-sre: I'll take this. Quick guess: NFS export with root_squash + container running as root -> chown/rm blocked. Which host/runner executed the job?

nina-ml: cleanup-runner-12 (us-west-2b). Cron is run by redwood-cron service account.

jessica-ops: I pushed an image change last week to drop root in the cleanup daemonset (runs as uid 1001) for security — maybe that mismatched expectations.

sam-eng: Trying a rerun now: `/opt/infra/scripts/cron_runner --job checkpoint-cleanup --run-id 20260314-03 --dry-run=false`

infra-bot: Action: rerun started (chk-20260314-03-rerun) by sam-eng — https://ci.redwood/s/34234

sam-eng: Rerun failed almost immediately with same error. Mount info from the runner:
````
$ mount | grep /mnt/checkpoints
server:/vol on /mnt/checkpoints type nfs (rw,relatime,vers=4.1,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,namlen=255,hard,proto=tcp,timeo=600,retrans=2,sec=sys,clientaddr=10.0.5.23,minorversion=1,addr=10.0.1.5,root_squash)
````
root_squash present. That matches the PermissionError.

kevin-sre: Confirmed. Our cleanup container expects to run as a UID that owns files (1001), but last image reconfigured processes to run as rootless in some paths. Options: 1) Change cron pod to run as uid 1001 so it can delete. 2) Make NFS export no_root_squash (infra ticket + approval). 3) Adjust cleanup logic to call `find ... -user 1001 -delete` (safer).

nina-ml: For immediate unblock can we skip deletion for the prefixes with the mismatch and do a manual S3 backup + manual deletion by ops?

sam-eng: I copied the affected checkpoints to s3://redwood-backups/checkpoint-20260314/ and removed the symlink pointers. Created tracker ISSUE-987 with the steps I took: https://tracker.redwood/ISSUE-987 — marking job disabled until fix.

jessica-ops: Sorry team — that image change was me. I can revert the daemonset to run as uid 1001 this afternoon, or we can update the cleanup script to be less privileged. Leaning revert + smaller cleanup patch.

kevin-sre: I'll open an infra ticket to evaluate NFS export change and run a bisect on the last two image changes to identify the exact commit that introduced the mismatch. Tentative plan in ticket: revert daemonset to uid 1001, add CI test that runs cleanup against an NFS mount with root_squash enabled.

nina-ml: Thanks — assigning Sam + Kevin to follow up. I'll re-enable cron once we have a fix validated. :thumbsup:

sam-eng: FYI I left a short note in the deploy logs so oncall can see the rollback plan.

kevin-sre: Adding one more note — if anyone needs to reproduce locally, mount the NFS export with `root_squash` and run the cleanup container as rootless to see the failure.

nina-ml: Great, appreciate the quick triage. I'll update the weekly postmortem with root cause and remediation items.

sam-eng: ping @kevin-sre when the infra ticket is up and I'll attach the bisect links.

kevin-sre: will do. :wave:
